terra.problem: “He's not impressed” states Isaiah's feeling as fact, though the text does not give it.
“Nobody hides in the middle of a busy courtyard” is an unsupported absolute claim.
A cookie telling an oven how to run a timer does not match the passage's reversal of maker and material.
The oven comparison does not clearly match the short time in the verse. Pulling out a batch that is already cooling on a rack is a confusing image.
The passage says the eyes of the blind will see; it does not say their eyes will open.
“Whoever is humble gets to enjoy that” turns the passage's statement about the humble into a promise to every humble person.
The joke contrasts looking for evil with hunting for a chocolate chip, making light of the serious evil in the passage.
The text says they look for evil; it does not say they are not also seeking peace.
“I can't make that one funny” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
“Pale faces turn back to normal” adds a detail. The LORD says Jacob's face will no longer grow pale.
The mustache joke makes the LORD's description of His work the setup for a joke, rather than keeping the humor on the human side.
The verse says Jacob sees his children around him. It does not say they see the work of God's hands.
The explanation equates questioning with grumbling and contrasts it with honoring God's name. The passage does not make those claims.
The joke compares the LORD's words with an unresponsive oven timer, making His words part of the punchline.
